relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: TRPV1 agonists (rutaecarpine, capsaicin and its derivatives, etc.) stimulate the secretion of CGRP and the antagonists inhibit the release of CGRP.

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: Activation of TRPV1 by protons leads to the upregulation of CGRP via calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) and CREB in dorsal root ganglion (DRG), while CGRP expression is reduced in TRPV1-deficient mice.

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: TRPV1-induced Ca2+ influx attenuated M1 macrophage polarization, as TRPV1 promoted the phosphorylation of CaMKII and facilitated the nuclear localization of nuclear factor-erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2), ultimately inhibiting M1 macrophage polarization.

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: TRPV1 activation can lead to the release of calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), substance P (SP), somatostatin, and other neurotransmitters

key_findings: Review: TRPV1 links nervous and immune systems by releasing neuropeptides (CGRP, SP) and driving Ca2+ influx in immune cells.
TRPV1-induced CGRP release is required for type 17 inflammation; TRPV1 Ca2+ signalling via CaMKII/Nrf2 restrains M1 macrophage polarization.
